motivation: v1 (results/kv-eviction-streaming-v1) ran once and failed its gate, but its full-cache baseline answered only 6/74 with 9 passages, so it could not measure eviction cost. v2 is a new experiment: shorter context, an explicit baseline-validity gate, and a query-aware method. v1 is kept unchanged.
hardware_scope: Apple Silicon GPU via MLX only; not CUDA, Ascend, phone or serving

data.construction: own passage + 2 seeded distractor passages, own passage at a seeded slot

eviction_point: once, after full-prompt prefill, before the first decode step

methods.stream: sink + recent window (same as v1), sink=4
methods.snapkv: observation window = last 32 prompt tokens; attention of window queries over earlier keys summed over window and the query heads of each KV group, max-pooled (kernel 7), top positions kept per KV head; window always kept; scored in NumPy (lab/snapkv.py)

metric: lab/qa_metrics.py score(): normalized EM, reported overall, answerable (is_impossible=false) and impossible separately

correctness_gate.description: (a) no-eviction EvictedKVCache path equals native greedy tokens and logits; (b) native decode with query capture enabled produces identical tokens and logits to capture disabled

baseline_gate.description: if full_cache answerable EM < 40%, the run stops after the full_cache quality pass and records baseline_invalid; no eviction quality or timing is reported

timing.order: arms shuffled per repeat with seed
timing.measured: decode wall time after eviction (prefill identical across arms, excluded); eviction copy time recorded separately

adoption_gate.note: Same thresholds as v1, frozen before any v2 run, applied to each eviction condition vs full_cache. n_answerable=33: one net lost answer fails the answerable gate. Eviction time (including NumPy scoring for SnapKV) is recorded but the speed gate uses decode time only, as in v1.

known_risks: 0.5B model may still be weak on 3-passage prompts; the baseline gate exists to stop rather than compare at the floor
SnapKV scoring adds prefill-side work not included in decode speed; it is reported separately
logical KV bytes are buffer sizes, not measured device memory
